newsitem.title: UK: UK's IMRO de-registers InterCapital AM executive.
newsitem.headline: UK's IMRO de-registers InterCapital AM executive.

text.p: UK regulatory body IMRO said it has terminated the registration of Geoffrey de Sibert, the former chief executive of InterCapital Asset Management.
A statement from the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation said de Sibert has agreed to a settlement of disciplinary proceedings brought against him by IMRO.

"Mr de Sibert did not exercise the integrity required of a registered Individual, from about April 1994 to March 1995, when he knowingly and deliberately overvalued warrants held by one of the funds managed by InterCapital," IMRO said.

The regulator said de Sibert "knew or should have known" his actions would cause the fund to be overvalued by between 2.25 million stg and 9.7 million stg, or up to 25 percent of the fund's correct valuation.
Investors joining the fund would be unfairly disadvantaged and those leaving unfairly advantaged. The fund would be unable to pay to all investors the perceived value of their holding.

IMRO said the breach meant the fund appeared to perform better than it had, and de Sibert had "deliberately failed to obtain the consent of the directors and auditors of the fund for his methods of valuing the warrants".

De Sibert was Chief Executive of InterCapital from February 1992 to March 1995. InterCapital was placed into a voluntary creditor's liquidation on April 4, 1995 and no longer conducts investment business.
De Sibert will pay IMRO's costs of 5,000 stg.
